restrictions: Ordinary collisions of the complete sha3-256-r5-prefix-v1 hash: zero IV, prefix rounds 0..4, SHA3 padding, full 256-bit digest; outputs are two distinct 135-byte messages (one padded block each, byte 135 = 0x86).

Phase A (deterministic, included in time and preprocessing): exhaustive blind search over CP-kernel alpha_3 of Hamming weight <= 10 with kernel alpha_4 and no digest-plane activity, then a CP-SAT feasibility screen for connector load w1 <= 140; outputs Guo et al. Trail core No. 3 as the unique usable trail.

Phase B (randomized): random best-probability beta_1, exact 2-round connector solved by CP-SAT with lazy relation cuts; at most K = 3 attempts, each killed by a hardware-counter watchdog after 1.60e+12 retired instructions; success when the realized solution space has dimension >= 41.
Phase C: Gray-code brute force over N = 2^39.6 pairs of the connector space with final recomputation of both complete hashes.
Costs: permutation calls at 1 unit; own C code by explicit operation counts; CP-SAT and Python by hardware-counted retired instructions times 1024 primitives per instruction.
Success probability 0.5 from conservative (95% lower) empirical estimates under heuristics H1 and H2; no nonuniform advice; memory bound includes code, solver and interpreter images.

heuristics.statement: For the connector space S output by Phase B, the pairs (x, x XOR alpha_0), x in S, collide independently with probability at least p_L = 2^-24 * R2_L * P34_L (95% lower bounds), so N = 2^39.6 enumerated pairs contain a collision with probability >= 1 - exp(-N p_L).
heuristics.scope: Spaces produced by connectors for Trail core No. 3; measured on 6 complete enumerations (2^30 to 2^38 pairs), including one space from the exact claimed Phase B, with round-2 hit rates and collision counts recorded per pair.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the measured spaces to the space produced by a fresh attempt, and from pooled frequency to a per-pair probability with Poisson tails.
heuristics.limitations: Empirical; 23 collision events in total. Pairs inside one space share most of their state structure, so independence is a modelling assumption. The per-space counts (1, 0, 2, 11, 8, 1) are consistent with it, but this does not prove it.

heuristics.statement: A Phase B attempt with fresh beta_1 coins succeeds (consistent system, DF >= 41, within the 1.60e+12-instruction budget) with probability at least r_L = 0.221, the Clopper-Pearson 95% lower bound from a hold-out batch run under the exact algorithm.
heuristics.scope: Hold-out batch of 30 attempts with fresh seeds, all included, run with the watchdog after the budget was fixed from a separate batch of 9; single-threaded solver; Apple M4 Pro.
heuristics.extrapolation: From the recorded attempts to the attempts of a fresh run; instruction counts from this CPU and library version.
heuristics.limitations: Empirical success rate. Instruction counts depend on the solver version (OR-Tools 9.15) and platform. The 1024 primitives-per-instruction bound is argued in Section 9.1, not measured.
